description: Hafnium is a lustrous, silvery gray, tetravalent transition metal with atomic number 72 and symbol Hf. It chemically resembles zirconium and is found in many zirconium minerals. The element is ductile and corrosion-resistant, forming a protective oxide film in air.
uses: Hafnium is most often used in alloys with nickel and was historically used in larger quantities to produce control rods for nuclear reactors due to its large neutron capture cross section. It is used in filaments and electrodes, and semiconductor fabrication processes use its oxide for integrated circuits at 45 nanometres and smaller, while superalloys can contain hafnium in combination with niobium, titanium, or tungsten.
characteristics: Hafnium is a shiny, silvery, ductile metal that is corrosion-resistant, changing from a hexagonal close-packed lattice to a body-centered cubic lattice at 2,388 K. Pure hafnium is extremely flammable and pyrophoric, capable of spontaneous combustion in air, and despite forming a protective oxide film, it is attacked by hydrofluoric acid and concentrated sulfuric acid. It has a notably higher density than zirconium and a high thermal neutron capture cross section roughly three orders of magnitude greater than that of zirconium.
